steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Odysseus returns to Ithaca disguised as a beggar by Athena's guidance — he must assess the situation before revealing himself

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Eumaeus the swineherd and Philoetius the cowherd remain loyal to Odysseus and help him against the suitors

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Odysseus and Telemachus plot the suitors' downfall together — father and son are reunited in secret

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Penelope sets the contest of the bow — only Odysseus can string his own great bow and shoot through twelve axes

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why does Odysseus disguise himself as a beggar rather than returning openly? | Q: What is the significance of the bow contest? | Q: How does Penelope test Odysseus's identity?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: To assess who remains loyal, understand the suitors' strength, and plan his revenge without being targeted. Athena advises this strategy — it uses cunning rather than direct confrontation. | Only Odysseus can string his own bow, proving his physical identity. The suitors cannot even bend it, showing their inferiority. Shooting through the twelve axes demonstrates unique skill that marks h | She mentions moving their marriage bed — but Odysseus knows it was built around a living olive tree and cannot be moved. This secret proves his identity more than any physical feat.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The recognition scene is the most important moment — analyse how identity is confirmed through knowledge, not just physical proof The immovable bed is the key symbol — it represents the unbreakable bond of marriage Compare the loyalty of Eumaeus with the disloyalty of the suitors and maidservants The violence of the revenge scene is shocking — be prepared to discuss whether it is justified Always link the homecoming to the wider themes of the poem: identity, loyalty, justice
